newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends higher on weather, outages.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends higher on weather, outages.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Tuesday, drawing strength from the short-term cash market which has been driven by strong energy demand in the Northwest and Rockies due to cooler-than-normal weather.
Unseasonably cool temperatures have also slowed the rate of snowmelt and reduced the amount of runoff into Northwest's vast hydroelectric system, market sources said.
Supply availability in the West was further tightened by a slate of plant outages. About 5,000 MW of generating capacity are reportedly off line for planned or unplanned repairs.
Keen buying interest in COB deliveries pulled PV values higher, market sources noted.
"Whatever you see in PV it's being driven by COB," said a Dallas-based futures trader.
Both May California-Oregon Border (COB) and Palo Verde (PV) futures contracts today posted their highest levels since the beginning of the year.
May COB finished up 43 cents at $12.05 a megawatt hour (MWh) after reaching a high of $12.20. June COB ended up 55 cents at at $12.20. Other COB months settled 15 to 38 cents higher.
May PV finished up 15 cents at $15.60 after traded between $15.40 and $15.70. June PV ended unchanged at $16.53. Other PV deliveries settled nine to 34 cents higher.
Day-ahead firm, peak electricity prices at COB climbed to $14.00-15.00 from yesterday's $13.50-14.00, while at PV stepped up to $15.25-15.75 from $15.00-15.50 Monday.
Brokers and traders said with market's focus on short term factors, the complex would test the upside again Wednesday.
The 1,073 MW Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear unit was expected to remain at 50 percent capacity until at least Wednesday morning, after being shut for unplanned repairs 11 days ago.
The 875 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Intermountain Power plant in Utah was shut Friday night for regular maintenance, which was expected to last through May 6.
A 750 MW unit at the Colstrip power plant in Montana was said to have been shut over the weekend for unplanned repairs, but the unit's status could not be confirmed.

Other out-of-service units included the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear unit in Washington state, a 750 MW unit at the Mohave coal-fired power plant in Nevada, a 550 MW unit at the Jim Bridger power plant in Wyoming, two 750 MW units at the Navajo plant in Arizona and a 300 MW unit at the Reid Gardner plant near Las Vegas.
In the Northwest, temperatures are expected to average near normal along the coast but five to 10 degrees Fahrenheit below normal in the eastern section today through Friday.
In the Southwest, forecasts called for cool weather with chances of mountain snow and valley rain Wednesday to Friday,
NYMEX estimated 687 COB and 531 PV contracts were sold, more than yesterday's 397 COB and 425 PV lots.
